findings.title: Release build points at placeholder .example domains
findings.explanation: The release API, upload, image, share-link, help and privacy-policy URLs all use reserved *.pennyjar.example hosts. Login, sync, account deletion and the privacy policy link will not work in a shipped build. Google Play also requires a working privacy policy URL. Replace these with the real production hosts.

findings.title: Auto Backup / device transfer include the receipts database, photos and plaintext CSV backup
findings.explanation: allowBackup is true. The rules exclude only the credentials, session and unlock SharedPreferences. They do not exclude receipts.db, which holds merchants, amounts and city. They also leave out files/receipts (receipt photos), files/backup/penny-jar-backup.csv (a plaintext export) and the settings and consent prefs. Financial and location data therefore goes to Google cloud backup and device transfer unencrypted by the app. The Keystore-wrapped notes become unreadable after a restore, and settings such as biometric_unlock restore without their keys. Exclude these paths, or set allowBackup to false.

findings.title: Biometric unlock is only a UI gate and does not protect the data
findings.explanation: The biometric-bound key only seals a random 32-byte secret that nothing uses. The session token and note keys are not tied to user authentication, and the database and photos are not encrypted. The lock is checked only at cold start, because the Locked screen is chosen only in the Starting LaunchedEffect. The app never relocks after backgrounding, and the lock can be bypassed on a rooted or instrumented device. Bind the token or data key to the biometric key and relock on resume if the app promises this protection.

findings.title: Data Safety form and privacy disclosures need review (analytics, location, financial data, account deletion)
findings.explanation: The app sends the following off-device. Mixpanel gets a user ID, usage events and expense bands, with automatic events enabled. The backend gets email, name, expense amounts, merchants, coarse-location city and receipt photos. The Play Data safety declaration must list all of this, including the third-party SDK, and match the privacy policy. The consent screen says only 'usage statistics' and does not mention the user ID or expense-derived properties. Play's account-deletion policy also requires a web URL for deletion requests in the Play Console, in addition to the in-app option. A human must confirm the declarations, because the code cannot show what is filed.
